## Setup

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
#| message: FALSE

# Load packages
library(terra)
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)
library(here)
library(sf)
library(stars)

# Set warnings to display as they occur
options(warn = 1)

# Set ggplot theme
set_theme(theme_bw())
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

# Load night lights rasters - 2/7/2021
vnp_07_1 <- read_stars(here('data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif'))
vnp_07_2 <- read_stars(here('data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif'))

# Load night lights rasters - 2/16/2021
vnp_16_1 <- read_stars(here('data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif'))
vnp_16_2 <- read_stars(here('data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif'))

# Load roads vector
# Use SQL query to only get rows where fclass = 'motorway'
roads <- sf::st_read(here('data', 'gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg'), query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")

# Load buildings vector
# Use SQL query to only get rows for residential buildings
builds <- sf::st_read(here('data', 'gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg'), query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")
```

## Data Merging

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

# Merge VNP 2/7 rasters
vnp_07_merged <- st_mosaic(vnp_07_1, vnp_07_2)

# Merge VNP 2/16 rasters
vnp_16_merged <- st_mosaic(vnp_16_1, vnp_16_2)
```

## Create blackout mask

```{r}
# Warning - confirm VNP rasters match before proceeding
# Note: compare crs, resolution, and extent for operations
print("Checking that VNP rasters match in CRS, resolution, and extent...")
if (st_crs(vnp_07_merged)$epsg == st_crs(vnp_16_merged)$epsg){
    # CRS match - true
    print("VNP CRS do match!")
    if (all(st_res(vnp_07_merged) == st_res(vnp_16_merged))){
        # Resolution match - true
        print("VNP Resolutions do match!")
        if (all(st_bbox(vnp_07_merged) == st_bbox(vnp_16_merged))) {
            # Extent match - true
            print("VNP Extents do match!")
            print("Success - VNP rasters match in all required characteristics for operations.")
        } else {
            # Extent match - false
            stop("VNP Extents do NOT match!")
        }
    } else {
        # Resolution match - false
        stop("VNP Resolutions do NOT match!")
    }
} else {
    # CRS match - false
    stop("VNP CRS do NOT match!")
}
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

# Create mask raster w/ the change (difference) in night light intensity
vnp_mask <- vnp_07_merged - vnp_16_merged
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

# Reclassify using stars::cut()
vnp_rcl <- cut(vnp_mask,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 200, Inf),
  labels = c("OK", "BLACKOUT"))

# Assign NA to cells with a diff <= 200 nW cm-2sr-1
vnp_rcl[vnp_rcl == "OK"] <- NA
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

vnp_rcl_v <- vnp_rcl |> 
    # Convert raster to vector
    st_as_sf() |> 
    # Fix invalid geometries
    st_make_valid()
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Create bbox for houston based on above coords
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(
    c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
    crs = st_crs(vnp_rcl_v))

# Crop vnp_rcl vector data to houston bbox
houston_mask_v <- st_crop(vnp_rcl_v, houston_bbox) |> 
    # Reproject to projected 2D crs EPSG:3083 (NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area)
    st_transform(crs = "EPSG:3083")
```

## Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask

```{r}
# Warning - confirm roads and houston_mask_v match before proceeding
print("Checking that houston_mask and roads vectors match CRS...")
if (!(st_crs(houston_mask_v) == st_crs(roads))){
    # CRS match - false
    warning("CRS do NOT match! Reprojecting roads to match EPSG:3083...")
    roads <- st_transform(roads, crs = st_crs(houston_mask_v))
    print("CRS reprojection complete.")
}
print("CRS do match!")
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

# Create 200m buffer around motorways in roads vector
motorway_buff <- roads |> 
    # Create the buffers
    st_buffer(dist = 200) |> 
    # Consolidate road and buffer geometries into one polygon to handle overlapping buffers
    st_union()
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Find geometries in houston_mask that do not intersect with motorway_buff
# st_difference - see Week 3 Lab
blackout_mask <- st_difference(houston_mask_v, motorway_buff)
```

## Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts

```{r}
# Warning - confirm builds and blackout_mask match before proceeding
print("Checking that blackout_mask and builds vectors match CRS...")
if (!(st_crs(blackout_mask) == st_crs(builds))){
    # CRS match - false
    warning("CRS do NOT match! Reprojecting builds to match EPSG:3083...")
    builds <- st_transform(builds, crs = st_crs(blackout_mask))
    print("CRS reprojection complete.")
}
print("CRS do match!")
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Find geometries in builds (residential polygons) that do intersect with blackout_mask
# st_filter, default = st_intersects - see Week 3 Lab
blackout_homes <- st_filter(builds, blackout_mask)

# Count number of residences (rows) impacted
num_blackout_homes <- nrow(blackout_homes)

# Confirm no duplicates:
# Number of unique IDs equals number of rows, should return TRUE
length(unique(blackout_homes$osm_id)) == nrow(blackout_homes)
```

## Generate Figures

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5

# Figure 1: Two maps comparing night light intensities before and after storms

# Crop merged vnp rasters to houston using above bbox
houston_07 <- st_crop(vnp_07_merged, houston_bbox)
houston_16 <- st_crop(vnp_16_merged, houston_bbox)

# Apply gamma correction in new rasters - 0.25 for VIIRS images
houston_07_gamma <- houston_07^0.25
houston_16_gamma <- houston_16^0.25

# Find min and max limits for both gamma rasters to use tm_scale_continuous below
# Note: [[1]] are needed to access pixel matrix within stars objects
min_lim = min(c(houston_07_gamma[[1]], houston_16_gamma[[1]]), na.rm = TRUE)
max_lim = max(c(houston_07_gamma[[1]], houston_16_gamma[[1]]), na.rm = TRUE)

# Create 07 Houston night lights map
houston_07_map <- tm_shape(houston_07_gamma) +
  tm_raster(col.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE), #Hide this legend
            # Change to continuous radiance scale
            col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
                # Change color scheme
                values = "inferno",
                # Set min and max gamma radiance values
                limits = c(min_lim,max_lim)
            )) +
  # Add compass
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.color = "white") +
  # Add scalebar
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.color = "white") +
  # Add title
  tm_title(text = "Houston Night Lights: Pre-Storm - February 7, 2021   ",
           size = 1.8) +
  # Set asp = 0 for PDF display
  tm_layout(asp = 0)

# Create 16 Houston night lights map
houston_16_map <- tm_shape(houston_16_gamma ) +
  tm_raster(col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Radiance^0.25\n(nW cm-2sr-1)",
                                   position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
            # Change to continuous radiance scale
            col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
                # Change color scheme
                values = "inferno",
                # Set min and max gamma radiance values
                limits = c(min_lim,max_lim)
            )) +
  # Add compass
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.color = "white") +
  # Add scalebar
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.color = "white") +
  # Add title
  tm_title(text = "Houston Night Lights: Post-Storm - February 16, 2021",
           size = 1.8) +
  # Set asp = 0 for PDF display
  tm_layout(asp = 0)

# Arrange maps as one figure
tmap_arrange(houston_07_map, houston_16_map, ncol = 2, widths = c(0.44, 0.56)) 
```
**Figure 1:** VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) NASA Earth satellite images of Houston, Texas night lights comparing pre-storm February 07, 2021 light radiance to post-storm February 16, 2021 light radiance. Pixel data is gamma corrected for display (radiance^0.25).

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

# Figure 2: Map of homes in Houston that lost power

blackout_map <- tm_basemap(server = "OpenStreetMap") +
    # Add blackout_homes on top of basemap as polygons
    tm_shape(blackout_homes) +
        tm_polygons(fill = "#3b0390", # Set fill color
                    fill_alpha = 0.5, # Set fill transparency
                    col = "#3b0390") + # Set border color
    # Add a legend
    tm_add_legend(
        # Set type of tmap objects
        type = "polygons",
        # Set polygons labels
        labels = c("Blackout-Affected Homes"),
        # Set polygon fill colors
        fill = c("#3b0390"),
        # Set polygon border colors
        col = c("#3b0390"),
        # Set legned title
        title = "Features:",
        # Set legend position
        position = tm_pos_out("right","center"),
        # Increase text size
        text.size = 1.1,
        # Increase title size
        title.size = 1.1
    ) +
    # Add compass
    tm_compass(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
    # Add scalebar
    tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
    # Add title
    tm_title("Houston Storm 2021: Blackout-Affected Homes") +
    # Set asp = 0 for PDF display
    tm_layout(asp = 0,
              # Adjust outer margin space in PDF
              outer.margins = c(0.1,0.1,0.1,0.1))

blackout_map
```
**Figure 2:** Map of Houston, Texas showing homes that experienced a blackout during the February 2021 storms (purple polygons), as detected by difference in night light radiance (>200 nW cm-2sr-1) in the comparison of pre-and post-storm VIIRS satellite imagery. Homes within 200m of motorways were excluded, as motorway radiance interferes with accurate blackout conclusions for those homes. OpenStreetMap is used as the basemap in this image to note motorway locations.

## Reflection

The storms in Houston, Texas between February 7 and 16, 2021 appear to have inflicted blackout conditions on many neighborhoods in the city. Comparing VIIRS night lights radiance imagery between the two dates above shows several areas in southern, northwest, and northeast Houston that were experiencing blackouts on February 16 (Figure 1). Also apparent are five locations of very high radiance in the later image - possibly due to flares captured by the satellite from oil and chemical factories in emergency mode (Wikipedia, 2021). In Figure 2, the difference in pre- and post-storm night light radiance was used to detect residences that were affected by power blackouts. Residences that were 1) over 200m from a motorway and 2) observed to have a greater than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 radiance difference were classified as having experienced a blackout - this count totalled 157,408 residential properties. Homes within 200m from a motorway were excluded, as motorway radiance could not be separated from residence radiance by VIIRS satellite. It should also be noted that this analysis relied on VIIRS satellite data from two moments in time on different days - more blackouts could have occured in Houston at different times that were not captured in this data.

## Data

Night Lights Data: NASA Level-1 and Atmosphere Archive and Distribution System (LAADS) DAAC. (2019). VIIRS/NPP Daily Gridded Day Night Band 500m Linear Lat Lon Grid Night (Collection 1) [Data set]. Goddard Space Flight Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/VIIRS/VNP46A1.001

Roads and Houses Data: OpenStreetMap contributors. (2021). Texas OpenStreetMap - roads and buildings [Data set]. Geofabrik. https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/texas.html

2021 Texas power crisis. (2021, October 2). In Wikipedia. Retrieved November 20, 2026, from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Texas_power_crisis
